svg.title: One surprise number versus a surprise map
svg.desc: On the left, a single big circle stands for one lump-sum surprise number that only tells you how surprised the model was. On the right, a grid of 12 body-part rows by 16 time columns shades some cells darker to show where the model was surprised. In the example the darker cells cluster on the right knee and right ankle rows, showing a one-sided pattern.
svg.text: One number tells you HOW surprised.
"Surprised" means the model expected one thing and the real movement did something else.
A grid: 12 body-part rows across 16 slices of time (a heatmap, meaning darker = more surprise).
time, 16 slices of one short clip, left to right
The dark cells cluster on the RIGHT knee and ankle: a one-sided pattern.
Same total surprise as the circle, but now you see WHERE and WHEN it happened.
less surprised, left, to more surprised, right.
Reminder: the model's own guess of a hidden joint, not a diagnosis.
